symptom: `mxcli test`: a test whose body does `call java action` cannot use `@throws` — the expected Java exception is reported as `ERROR <message>`, not PASS; without `@throws` it is also ERROR rather than the usual `FAIL exception during execution: …`
cause: The runner attaches its `ON ERROR` handler only to statements matched by `containsCallMicroflow`, which recognised `CALL MICROFLOW` / `CALL NANOFLOW` only; every other call-shaped activity was emitted without a handler and its error escaped the generated test microflow to the endpoint's outer handler
insight: The set of statements the runner wraps must be the set the grammar gives `onErrorClause` to (MDLMicroflow.g4) — enumerate it from there, not from the statements the first tests used. Unit test each kind through BOTH generators and `visitor.Build` the output, since an `ON ERROR` on a statement that cannot take one would be a parse error. The cheap workaround (wrap the call in a microflow) hides the gap, so it went unreported until a module's own Java actions were tested. Proven live on 11.12.1 `--local --db-type hsqldb`: unfixed binary ERROR/ERROR, fixed PASS/FAIL on the same project. Also anchored the match at the statement start — the old `strings.Contains` treated a LOG whose text mentioned `call microflow` as a call
